en.name: Canned tuna
en.summary: An unopened can of tuna keeps 3 years in the cupboard. That figure belongs to the sealed can alone — once it is opened, tuna is a highly perishable refrigerated food and should be covered, chilled and eaten within a couple of days.
en.pantry: Cool, dry and dark, 3 years. Canned tuna is a low-acid food made safe by commercial sterilisation inside an intact seal, so the can itself is the thing to inspect. Discard, unopened and untasted, any can that is bulging, leaking, rusted through at a seam, deeply dented on the seam or rim, or that hisses, foams or spurts when you pierce it — those are the classic signs of a failed seal, and in home-canned low-acid fish they are the warning signs for botulism. Store cans off a damp floor; rust starts a chain that ends in a hole.
en.fridge: Once opened, a can of tuna is ready-to-eat perishable fish: cover it, refrigerate at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, and use it within a couple of days at most. The leftovers do not need to leave the can for safety, but they should for flavour — tinned fish picks up a sharp metallic edge from the exposed cut metal within hours. Do not leave an opened can standing out for more than two hours, or one hour above 32 °C (90 °F).
en.freezer: No freezer timeline is published for canned tuna, and freezing it after opening is not worth doing. The fish has already been cooked to sterility in the can, so the flakes are fragile; freezing breaks them down further and they thaw dry and woolly with a watery liquid around them. Buy can sizes you will finish, or cook the leftovers into something — a pasta bake, fish cakes, a rice dish — and store that as a cooked dish instead.
spoilage: A bulging, leaking or seam-dented can, or one that hisses, foams or spurts when opened.
A sharp ammonia-like, sour or putrid smell on opening.
Milky, cloudy or ropy liquid in the can.
Flesh that is mushy, slimy, or grey-green rather than pale pink or beige.
tips: Decant leftovers into a covered container as soon as the can is open.
Buy smaller cans if a whole one is more than a meal.
Rotate cans front to back and keep the store dry.
Never taste a suspect can — a bulging or spurting can goes straight in the bin.

faq.q: How long does canned tuna keep?
faq.a: 3 years unopened in a cool dry cupboard. Once opened, cover it, refrigerate at 4 °C (40 °F) or below and use it within a couple of days.

faq.q: Can you keep opened tuna in the can?
faq.a: It is safe to, but the fish takes on a metallic taste quickly. Transfer it to a covered container.

faq.q: What if the can is bulging?
faq.a: Throw it away without opening or tasting it. A bulging, leaking or spurting low-acid can is the classic sign of a failed seal.

zh.name: 鮪魚罐頭
zh.summary: 未開封的鮪魚罐頭放櫥櫃可放 3 年。這個數字只屬於密封的罐體——一旦開罐，鮪魚就是非常容易腐敗的冷藏食品，必須加蓋冷藏，並在一兩天內吃完。
zh.pantry: 陰涼、乾燥、避光，3 年。鮪魚罐頭是低酸性食品，安全性靠的是完好密封內的商業滅菌，所以真正該檢查的是罐體本身。罐身膨脹、滲漏、接縫鏽穿、接縫或捲封處嚴重凹陷，或穿刺時洩氣、冒泡、噴汁的，請不要打開、不要試吃，直接丟棄——這些是密封失效的典型徵兆，而在自家醃製的低酸性魚產品上，它們就是肉毒桿菌的警訊。罐頭不要放在潮濕地面，一旦開始生鏽，接下來就是穿孔。
zh.fridge: 開罐後的鮪魚就是即食的易腐魚肉：請加蓋、冷藏在 4 °C 以下，最多一兩天內用完。剩下的就安全而言不一定要離開罐子，但為了味道應該離開——裸露的切口金屬幾小時內就會讓魚肉帶明顯的金屬味。開過的罐子放在室溫不要超過兩小時，氣溫超過 32 °C 時不要超過一小時。
zh.freezer: 鮪魚罐頭沒有公布的冷凍期限，開罐後拿去冷凍也不值得。罐內的魚肉已經被加熱到滅菌程度，肉絲本來就脆弱；冷凍會讓它進一步崩解，解凍後又乾又柴、周圍還積一層水。請買吃得完的容量，或把剩料煮成一道菜——焗烤義大利麵、魚餅、拌飯——之後照那道熟食來保存。
spoilage: 罐身膨脹、滲漏或接縫凹陷，或開罐時洩氣、冒泡、噴汁。
開罐即聞到刺鼻氨味、酸味或腐臭味。
罐內湯汁乳白、混濁或牽絲。
魚肉軟爛、黏滑，或呈灰綠色而不是淡粉或米色。
tips: 一開罐就把剩料換到加蓋容器。
一罐吃不完就改買小罐。
罐頭由前往後輪替，存放處保持乾燥。
可疑的罐頭不要試吃——膨脹或噴汁就直接丟。

faq.a: 未開封放陰涼乾燥的櫥櫃 3 年。開罐後加蓋冷藏在 4 °C 以下，一兩天內用完。

faq.q: 開過的鮪魚可以留在罐子裡嗎？
faq.a: 安全上可以，但魚肉很快就會有金屬味。請換到加蓋容器。
不要打開、不要試吃，直接丟棄。低酸性罐頭膨脹、滲漏或噴汁，是密封失效的典型徵兆。
